title: Your client wants AI. How do you scope the implementation?
audience: Implementation firm with a client seeking broader AI capability
reader_need: How do we scope the client request without overlooking the work around it?
contribution: Form the work behind the request and divide responsibility with the implementation partner.
evidence_boundary: E1 supports the end-client situation. Direct partner search demand remains unvalidated.

title: Who can help connect the AI tools we already bought?
audience: Founder, COO or transformation leader connecting departments
reader_need: How can our existing systems and AI work together?
contribution: Follow the business goal through people, systems and decisions; define a complete first implementation.
evidence_boundary: E1 directly describes connecting teams; E2 supports tool frustration. Neither establishes exact-query volume.

title: How do you move an AI onboarding pilot into actual operations?
audience: Operations owner accountable for the customer-to-service chain
reader_need: The pilot works, but can the delivery team actually take over?
contribution: Define readiness from the receiving team’s needs and preserve commitments through the handoff.
evidence_boundary: Specific onboarding search intent is an editorial hypothesis. It illustrates the broader connected operation.

title: How do you turn AI sales research into a useful CRM handoff?
audience: Commercial leader responsible for research through follow-up
reader_need: The AI finds information, but sales still has to redo the work.
contribution: Carry evidence, uncertainty, current account history and an owned next action.
evidence_boundary: E2 supports customer-acquisition/tool overload; the precise CRM handoff query is unvalidated.

title: Why do AI workflows break when requirements change?
audience: Operations owner or implementation leader maintaining AI work
reader_need: Why do corrections disappear and handoffs need rescuing?
contribution: Preserve the accepted state, show what changed and update the work that depends on it.
evidence_boundary: E4 supports coordination burden. Exact business repair demand is unvalidated.

title: What should AI implementation include besides the model or agent?
audience: Business sponsor choosing a delivery approach
reader_need: Who should help us implement AI, and what should we expect them to deliver?
contribution: Compare a complete first operation, responsibilities, ongoing support and full cost.
evidence_boundary: Qualitative provider-selection question observed; no ranking, keyword volume or GR conversion data.

title: "What is it talking about?" How AI drifts
audience: Business owner, operations leader, implementation practitioner or curious AI user
entrance: Recognizable AI question or experience; topical interest
reader_need: "What is it talking about?" How AI drifts
contribution: Source-grounded interpretation, causes, ways to catch or limit the failure, and a productive next step.
evidence_boundary: Primary research establishes the topic and bounded findings. Exact search volume, popularity rank, headline response and buyer fit are unmeasured.
